entity.name: Albert Einstein
entity.description: The patent clerk who reimagined the universe. A German-born physicist who published four papers in a single year that overturned classical physics, introduced E = mc², and predicted that gravity bends light. He fled Nazi Germany, urged Roosevelt to pursue atomic research, and spent his final decades chasing a unified theory that eluded him.

story.name: Albert Einstein
story.description: A patent clerk publishes four papers that shatter classical physics, predicts gravity bends light and is proved right by a solar eclipse, signs a letter that launches the atomic age, and dies still scribbling equations in a Princeton hospital bed.

moments.name: Albert Einstein Is Born in the Kingdom of Württemberg
moments.subtitle: His parents worry he has a learning disability because he is so slow to speak
moments.description: The house at Bahnhofstraße 20 in Ulm, a modest dwelling in the shadow of the city's towering Gothic minster, was where Hermann and Pauline Einstein welcomed their first child on 14 March 1879. The infant Albert was so slow to begin talking that his parents feared a learning disability. At five, sick in bed in the family's new Munich home, the boy received a compass from his father — and the invisible force steering the needle ignited a fascination with physics that never faded. By twelve he was teaching himself calculus; by fourteen he claimed to have mastered integral and differential calculus entirely on his own.

moments.name: Einstein Publishes Four Papers That Overthrow Classical Physics
moments.subtitle: A 26-year-old patent clerk rewrites the rules of space, time, matter, and energy in one year
moments.description: From a small desk at the Swiss Federal Patent Office in Bern — a second-floor hall where Einstein spent his days evaluating technical applications — the 26-year-old clerk produced four papers in 1905 that shattered the foundations of physics. One explained the photoelectric effect by proposing light comes in quanta. Another proved atoms exist by explaining Brownian motion. A third introduced special relativity, abolishing absolute time. The fourth derived E = mc², showing mass and energy are interchangeable. He had no lab, no research assistants, and no academic position.

moments.name: Einstein Presents General Relativity to the Prussian Academy
moments.subtitle: Ten years of struggle to extend special relativity finally yields a theory of gravity itself
moments.description: Inside the neoclassical halls of the Prussian Academy of Sciences on Unter den Linden in Berlin, Einstein delivered four lectures in November 1915 presenting his general theory of relativity. The theory replaced Newton's gravitational force with the curvature of spacetime itself, predicting that massive objects warp the geometry of the universe around them. Einstein had spent a decade wrestling with the mathematics, enlisting classmate Marcel Grossmann to help him master tensor calculus. Four years later, a solar eclipse expedition confirmed his prediction that starlight bends around the sun.

moments.name: Einstein Signs a Letter Warning Roosevelt About German Nuclear Weapons
moments.subtitle: The pacifist physicist helps launch the most destructive weapon program in history
moments.description: A lifelong pacifist put his signature to a document that would help birth the atomic age. In August 1939, at a rented cottage on Nassau Point in Peconic, Long Island — a quiet retreat overlooking the bay — Einstein signed a letter drafted by Leo Szilard warning President Roosevelt that Nazi Germany might develop nuclear weapons. The letter urged the United States to begin uranium research. Roosevelt created an advisory committee that evolved into the Manhattan Project. Einstein himself was denied security clearance to work on it. He later called signing the letter the greatest mistake of his life.
moments.address: Nassau Point, Peconic, Long Island, New York

moments.name: Einstein Wins the Nobel Prize — Not for Relativity
moments.subtitle: The committee honors his safest work and ignores the theory that remade physics
moments.description: The Nobel Committee at Stockholm's Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences awarded Einstein the 1921 Nobel Prize in Physics — announced in November 1922 — not for relativity but for the photoelectric effect, a safer choice. Einstein was not in Stockholm to collect it; he was on a steamship to Japan and received the news by telegram. As part of his divorce settlement with first wife Mileva Maric, he had agreed to hand over his Nobel money to her. The 121,572 Swedish kronor went to Maric, who used part of it to buy three apartment buildings in Zurich.
moments.address: Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences, Stockholm, Sweden

moments.name: Einstein Dies with Unfinished Equations on His Nightstand
moments.subtitle: A pathologist steals his brain hours later without the family's permission
moments.description: Albert Einstein died at Princeton Hospital in New Jersey in the early morning of 18 April 1955, at age seventy-six. An abdominal aortic aneurysm had ruptured; he refused surgery, saying he wanted to go when he wanted to go. On the nightstand beside his hospital bed lay pages of unfinished calculations — his latest attempt at a unified field theory merging gravity and electromagnetism. Within hours, pathologist Thomas Harvey removed Einstein's brain during the autopsy without the family's permission. Harvey kept it in jars for over forty years, parceling out slices to researchers.
